let namedReferences: Map<string, string> | undefined;

/** The characters a reference name stands for; the table is read on first use. */
function namedReference(name: string): string | undefined {
  if (namedReferences === undefined) {
    namedReferences = new Map();
    for (const entry of NAMED_REFERENCES.split(' ')) {
      const separator = entry.indexOf('=');
      const codePoints = entry
        .slice(separator + 1)
        .split(',')
        .map(hex => parseInt(hex, 16));
      namedReferences.set(
        entry.slice(0, separator),
        String.fromCodePoint(...codePoints),
      );
    }
  }
  return namedReferences.get(name);
}

// `&name;`, `&#digits;`, or `&#xhex;` (CommonMark 0.31, entity and numeric
// character references). The longest HTML name is 31 characters.
const CHARACTER_REFERENCE =
  /^&(?:#[xX]([0-9a-fA-F]{1,6})|#([0-9]{1,7})|([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,31}));/;

/**
 * Matches a character reference starting at `start`. Returns the characters it
 * names and the index after it, or null when the text there is not a
 * reference: an unknown name, a missing `;`, or too many digits.
 */
export function matchCharacterReference(
  text: string,
  start: number,
): {value: string; end: number} | null {
  const match = CHARACTER_REFERENCE.exec(text.slice(start, start + 40));
  if (match == null) {
    return null;
  }
  const [reference, hex, decimal, name] = match;
  const end = start + reference.length;
  if (name != null) {
    const value = namedReference(name);
    return value === undefined ? null : {value, end};
  }
  const codePoint =
    hex != null ? parseInt(hex, 16) : parseInt(decimal ?? '0', 10);
  // NUL, surrogates, and values past Unicode become the replacement character.
  const isValid =
    codePoint !== 0 &&
    codePoint <= 0x10ffff &&
    (codePoint < 0xd800 || codePoint > 0xdfff);
  return {value: isValid ? String.fromCodePoint(codePoint) : '\uFFFD', end};
}

/** The characters a backslash escapes: ASCII punctuation (CommonMark 0.31). */
export function isAsciiPunctuation(character: string | undefined): boolean {
  return character != null && /^[!-/:-@[-`{-~]$/.test(character);
}

/**
 * Resolves backslash escapes and character references the way inline parsing
 * does, for text that is shown as written rather than parsed as Markdown, such
 * as an image's alt text. An escaped `&` stays literal.
 */
export function decodeLiteralText(text: string): string {
  if (!text.includes('\\') && !text.includes('&')) {
    return text;
  }
  let output = '';
  let index = 0;
  while (index < text.length) {
    const character = text[index];
    if (
      character === '\\' &&
      index + 1 < text.length &&
      isAsciiPunctuation(text[index + 1])
    ) {
      output += text[index + 1];
      index += 2;
      continue;
    }
    if (character === '&') {
      const reference = matchCharacterReference(text, index);
      if (reference != null) {
        output += reference.value;
        index = reference.end;
        continue;
      }
    }
    output += character;
    index++;
  }
  return output;
}

/**
 * Returns `text` with every valid named or numeric character reference
 * replaced by the characters it names, as Markdown renders it: `©`,
 * `©`, and `©` all become `©`, and a numeric reference to NUL, a
 * surrogate, or a code point past U+10FFFF becomes U+FFFD. An unknown name, a
 * reference without its `;`, and all other text stay as written.
 *
 * It works on plain text and knows nothing of Markdown, so the caller decides
 * where it applies: keep backslash-escaped references and code literal by not
 * passing them in (spec:AST-061 DEC-5).
 *
 * @example
 * ```
 * decodeMarkdownCharacterReferences('Fish & chips © 2026'); // 'Fish & chips © 2026'
 * decodeMarkdownCharacterReferences('&unknown; &copy'); // '&unknown; &copy'
 * ```
 */
export function decodeMarkdownCharacterReferences(text: string): string {
  let output = '';
  let index = 0;
  let ampersand = text.indexOf('&');
  while (ampersand !== -1) {
    const reference = matchCharacterReference(text, ampersand);
    if (reference == null) {
      ampersand = text.indexOf('&', ampersand + 1);
      continue;
    }
    output += text.slice(index, ampersand) + reference.value;
    index = reference.end;
    ampersand = text.indexOf('&', index);
  }
  return index === 0 ? text : output + text.slice(index);
}
